decision_reason: The test-only repair is bounded to three proptest bodies (lines 195-218, 222-238, 242-256). The proptest framework is the natural verifier; the test bodies are themselves the proof. The 128-case budget per proptest provides randomized coverage at the right granularity for a P1 repair.

The decoder at crates/vb_storage/src/keys.rs:346-434 is a pure match-based function with no loops, recursion, or unsafe indexing. Kani on a match-only decoder would reduce to pattern exhaustiveness, not a security-grade proof. A future Kani harness is captured in PS-MAL-019 (proof-seeds.jsonl) as out-of-scope follow-up for a future bead; this P1 is bounded to test-only proptest bodies.

The PO-008 proptest bodies are single-threaded. No Arc, Mutex, channels, or Send/Sync markers in the test scope. Proptest seeds run sequentially on the proptest framework's scheduler. No concurrent memory ordering or interleaving properties are in scope.

decision_reason: The truncate_len strategy declared on the action test signature must drive the truncated-payload constructor; the resulting decoder call must produce Err(KeyLengthMismatch { prefix: 0x32, expected: 13, actual: <short_len> }). The proptest body is the proof; the strategy input is consumed by the body, not discarded with _. Proptest's 128-case budget with failure_persistence: None surfaces the minimal failing case if the strategy is unwired.

The _extra_bytes strategy declared on the status and workflow test signatures must drive the oversize-payload constructor; the resulting decoder call must produce Err(KeyLengthMismatch { prefix: <actual_prefix>, expected: <18|13>, actual: <18|13 + extra> }). The repair removes the leading underscore so cargo clippy's unused_variables lint and proptest's strategy-consumption check both fire if the strategy is unwired.

Each of the three PO-008 tests must include a valid-length payload with run == 0 and assert Err(KeyDecodeError::InvalidRunId) for the matching side-index variant (IndexAction at keys.rs:423-425, IndexWorkflow at keys.rs:412-414, IndexStatus at keys.rs:400-402). The proptest body is the proof; the per-variant decoder branch is exercised by the prop_assert! on the typed variant.

All assertions must target KeyDecodeError variants (EmptyKey, UnknownPrefix, KeyLengthMismatch, InvalidRunId); assertions on JournalError::KeyCapacity (encoder-side error) and KeyDecodeError::ReservedSeqSentinel (unreachable from side-index payloads) are forbidden. The proptest body's prop_assert!(matches!(...)) is the static check on the typed-error vocabulary; clippy -D warnings will fail if the body uses a non-existent variant.

Tests must not assert on KeyDecodeError::ReservedSeqSentinel because the three side-index variants do not carry an EventSeq field. The proptest body's pattern-match is the static check; cargo clippy -D warnings will fail the build if the body adds a ReservedSeqSentinel arm against a side-index payload.

Decoder results must be matched under prop_assert!, never unwrapped or expected. The decoder is allowed to return Err and the test must not panic on that path. The cargo clippy -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D clippy::panic gate enforces this at compile time; proptest's prop_assert! macro propagates failures as proptest-shaped TestCaseError rather than panicking.

The PO-008 block must call decode_storage_key (and/or try_key_prefix) directly; routing through FjallJournal::has_*_index_entry is forbidden because those are membership-only probes that never decode. The proptest body's import graph is the static check — a body that imports FjallJournal::has_*_index_entry will fail cargo clippy's unused_imports lint (since the membership probe would be unused inside PO-008, which is forbidden to call).

Every proptest strategy declared on a PO-008 test signature must drive at least one malformed-payload shape; discarding with underscore is forbidden. The leading-underscore _extra_bytes and _short_key patterns in the current code (lines 213, 226, 245) are dead proptest strategies; the repair removes the underscore. cargo clippy's unused_variables lint enforces this at compile time.

Literal prefix bytes (0x30, 0x31, 0x32) and length envelopes (18, 13) used in malformed-payload construction must cite crates/vb_storage/src/constants.rs:38-43, 77-79 in a comment so future drift is detectable. The proptest body comment is the static check; a future bead may add pub re-exports, but the P1 uses literal constants per the type-contracts.md note.

KeyLengthMismatch assertions must specify the correct prefix byte per the actual first byte of the malformed payload; the decoder surfaces the actual prefix in KeyLengthMismatch { prefix, .. } at keys.rs:351, not the expected prefix. The proptest body's matches! pattern with the field surfacing is the static check; a body that uses prefix: <expected_prefix> for a <wrong_prefix> payload will fail proptest's prop_assert! at the variant level.

The truncated-slice length must stay in [1, 13) for action/workflow tests and [1, 18) for status tests so the assertion maps to KeyLengthMismatch rather than EmptyKey. The existing 1u8..=12u8 bound for the action test already satisfies this; status/workflow must use an analogous bound when truncating. The proptest strategy bound is the static check; widening the bound would shift the truncated slice to 0-length and the test would report EmptyKey mismatch (visible in failure output).

IndexAction / IndexWorkflow / IndexStatus decoder InvalidRunId branches at keys.rs:400-402, 412-414, 423-425 are exercised by the three PO-008 tests respectively. The proptest body's zero-run payload for each variant is the static check; the per-variant decoder branch coverage is closed at the proptest level.

Each of the three PO-008 tests must include a within-family-prefix-mismatch payload so the decoder's KeyLengthMismatch { prefix: <actual_prefix> } field surfacing is field-checked across all three side-index prefixes (0x30, 0x31, 0x32). The proptest body's within-family-mismatch payload is the static check; the field-level prefix surfacing at keys.rs:351 is verified by the matches! pattern with the actual prefix byte.

At least one PO-008 test asserts on KeyDecodeError::EmptyKey against an empty slice via try_key_prefix (or decode_storage_key). The proptest body's empty-slice call is the static check; the EmptyKey branch at keys.rs:282 is exercised by the prop_assert!.

At least one PO-008 test asserts on KeyDecodeError::UnknownPrefix { prefix: 0xFF } against a payload whose first byte is not one of the nine known prefixes. The proptest body's unknown-prefix payload is the static check; the UnknownPrefix branch at keys.rs:293 is exercised by the prop_assert!.

JOURNAL_KEY_PROPTEST_CASES = 128 at journal_side_index_contracts.rs:23 is preserved; the repair does not raise or lower the case count. The constant is the static check; cargo nextest run output reports 128 cases per proptest, and any drift is observable in the test report.

The file-level #![forbid(unsafe_code)] lint is preserved; the repair adds no unsafe and respects Holzman-Rust zero-tolerance linting. The file-level lint is the static check; cargo clippy -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D clippy::panic enforces the zero-tolerance policy at compile time, and rustc rejects unsafe under forbid(unsafe_code) before clippy runs.
